chunks: And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, who raised it (traced it back to the Prophet), he said:
Whoever comes to one who has introduced an innovation and glorifies him, he is indeed working toward the demolition of Islam.

key_terms.بِدْعَة: bid'ah — a blameworthy innovation in religion, introducing something not sanctioned by the Prophet or Imams
key_terms.تَعْظِيم: glorification, reverence — here meaning social endorsement or showing honor to an innovator
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: marfu' — a hadith chain raised (attributed) directly to the Prophet (SAWW) without naming all intermediaries
key_terms.هَدْم: demolition, tearing down — used metaphorically for the structural undermining of the religion

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Islam on honoring someone who introduces religious innovations (bid'ah)?
ai.summary: This hadith delivers a stern warning about the social reinforcement of religious innovations (bid'ah). The Imam teaches that not only the innovator but also those who venerate, endorse, or associate respectfully with innovators are complicit in undermining Islam's integrity. In early Shia scholarly circles, bid'ah referred specifically to introducing doctrinal or ritual elements without prophetic or Imamic sanction — and glorifying such a person was seen as legitimizing their harmful innovation.
word_analysis: he raised it (traced it back to the Prophet)
